messages:
perf-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 2s on /v1/generate (hosted-prod) since 18:32 UTC. p95 also elevated. Rolling window: 15m.
perf-bot: metrics: p99=2.7s, p95=1.2s, requests=12k, error_rate=0.2%. KV cache hit rate: 51% -> dropped from 98% at 17:50.
marta: seeing this too on dashboard. p99 spike coincides with the 17:45 deploy (deploy sha: 8f3b2c7). Anyone already looking? @kevin @ashley
kevin: I'm on it. Quick check: cache misses spike aligns with traffic to model: rtx-13-quant. Looks like KV prefix cache miss rate jumped to 48% (was <5%).
ashley: interesting — did we change cache key shape in that PR? I remember a serialization tweak to support request-level metadata. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4123
kevin: opening logs.
kevin: logs show a lot of unique cache keys around prefix: 
```
kv_key: model:rtx-13-quant:prefix:conv_v2:user_session=6a1b2c3d:prompt_hash=ab12...
kv_key: model:rtx-13-quant:prefix:conv_v2:user_session=9f8d7e1a:prompt_hash=ab12...
```
kevin: that user_session field shouldn't be part of the cache key — that effectively makes prefix cache per-session and causes thrash.
marta: omg that explains it. The PR added `request.session_id` into the cache key concat by accident while trying to namespace ephemeral contexts.
devon: confirmed locally: if session_id varies per-request, we get near-zero reuse. Repro steps I used: 
1) run load: `ab -n 1000 -c 40 http://localhost:8080/v1/generate` with unique session_id per request
2) curl /admin/cache/stats -> shows miss_rate ~96%
3) revert key shape to remove session_id -> miss_rate back to ~4%

ashley: can we hotfix without full rollback? Maybe strip session_id at cache key generation path and deploy small patch.
kevin: I can patch and push a canary to a single region. Quick mitigation plan:
- 17:58: revert cache-key change in a small hotfix (patch branch) -> patch id: hotfix/kv-key-fix
- 18:05: deploy canary to us-west-2 (10% traffic) and monitor cache hit rate
- 18:20: if stable, roll to 100%
- add durable fallback: if miss_rate > 20% for model route, temporarily pin routing to previous model variant (rtx-13-quant:v202)

sre-oncall: also recommend increasing warmup for new model variants during rollout. Right now warmup is 0 for quant variants; set warmup_count=100 for first 5 minutes to populate KV caches.
marta: I pushed a config change to k8s configmap to bump warmup: `models.rtx-13-quant.warmup_count: 100` and a patch to keygen removing session_id. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4140
ashley: logs after canary deploy (18:12): cache hit rate jumped to 86% in canary region, p99 in canary down to 900ms. Global still higher due to remaining regions.
kevin: rolling 100% now. Also added a short TTL to prefix entries to prevent long-term pollution while we're unsure of key correctness: `prefix.ttl_seconds: 600`
marta: monitoring graph: global p95 down from 1.2s -> 800ms, p99 from 2.7s -> 1.0s over 30m. Miss rate back to ~7%.
devon: root cause summary to add to postmortem: accidental inclusion of ephemeral `session_id` in cache key serialization introduced in PR 4123. That turned prefix cache into per-session cache -> catastrophic reduction in reuse -> p95/p99 regressions.
kevin: follow-ups:
- revert commit permanently and add unit tests for cache key canonicalization (hash-normalized fields only).
- add CI fuzz test: generate many random request metadata shapes and assert stable cache key for semantically-equivalent requests.
- add alert: `kv_prefix_miss_rate > 10% for 5m` -> page SRE.
- instrumentation: emit `cache_key_components` metric (enum) to help detect inclusion of high-cardinality fields (session_id, request_id).
ashley: also put a guard in runtime: if a generated cache key has > 8 unique variable components or length > 1024, mark key as suspicious and increment `cache_key_suspect` counter, avoid writing to cache for that request to prevent thrash.
sre-oncall: adding incident note in incidents/ later. We should also notify support and affected customers list. Any billing or auth impacts?
marta: no billing/auth impact reported. Support ticket #2341 opened for customers that pinged latency. I'll update them: root cause identified + fix deployed + ongoing monitoring.
kevin: command snippets used during triage: 
- check cache stats: `curl -sS http://admin-host:9000/admin/cache/stats | jq .`
- inspect keys: `redis-cli --scan | grep rtx-13-quant | head -n 50`
- rollback variant routing: `rbacctl set-route generate --model rtx-13-quant:v202`

devon: note for postmortem: we should include timeline and a small snippet of offending code for audit: 
```
// bad: included ephemeral session id
String key = join(":", model, prefixName, request.context.session_id, promptHash);
// good: canonicalize session -> use static user_namespace only
String key = join(":", model, prefixName, canonicalizeUser(request.context.user_id), promptHash);
```
marta: next actions assigned:
- kevin: follow-up PR with tests + deploy by EOD (assignee)
- ashley: create alert and dashboard tweak for `cache_key_suspect` and miss rate (assignee)
- devon: add warmup config to rollout playbook + update runbook (assignee)
- sre-oncall: write incident stub + customer notes (assignee)

kevin: opened PR 4145 with test cases. Can someone review quickly? @ashley @marta
ashley: reviewing now. LGTM, will merge after smoke.
marta: thanks everyone. I'll file the postmortem skeleton and ping legal if customers request SLA credits. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: RESOLVED: p99 back within SLO (checked 30m window). Incident closed pending postmortem.
